ev.v_wine_symposium.title: The Scythian Way
ev.v_wine_symposium.text: At the banquet the master of the drinking ordered the wine served unmixed — 'the Scythian way.' Anyone who reaches for the water jug gets laughed at, and the cup goes round faster and faster.
ev.v_wine_symposium.text.rome: At a rich neighbour's dinner the wine comes neat, with no water: the host is showing off his Falernian. Anyone who waters it down is loudly called a yokel.
ev.v_wine_symposium.text.egypt: At the festival of Hathor custom says you drink until you're drunk — it is the Feast of Drunkenness. The jars never run dry before dawn, and no one counts your cups.
ev.v_wine_symposium.neat: Drink it neat like everyone else
ev.v_wine_symposium.neat.ok: Your head spun, light and sweet. The morning was worse, but by evening you wanted it again.
ev.v_wine_symposium.mixed: Mix it with water, as the elders did
ev.v_wine_symposium.mixed.ok: They laughed at you, but next morning the mockers were nursing their heads while you got up fresh.
ev.v_wine_symposium.leave.ok: You left when the cup-dancing began. The walk home was quiet and full of stars.
ev.v_wine_grief.title: A Cup Against Sorrow
ev.v_wine_grief.text: It has been a hard year, and in the evenings your feet carry you to the corner tavern on their own. The owner pours without asking, and after the third cup the noise inside you quiets down.
ev.v_wine_grief.drown.ok: The tavern became a second home. The sorrow didn't leave — it just waits for you in the mornings.
ev.v_wine_grief.friend: Go to a friend and talk it out
ev.v_wine_grief.friend.ok: You sat up until dawn, and more words were spent than wine. It helped.
ev.v_wine_grief.temple: Go to the temple instead of the tavern
ev.v_wine_grief.temple.ok: The temple is cool and smells of incense. You stayed until dark and walked home sober.
ev.v_wine_grief.work.ok: You work until you drop and fall asleep before the sadness can catch you. Not a cure, but a breather.
ev.v_wine_tavern.text.1: You woke on a bench by a stranger's door, without your cloak and without any memory of last night. The neighbours look away.
ev.v_wine_tavern.text.2: At the tavern you sang louder than anyone, then argued with the owner about your tab. Nobody remembers who was right, but you were the one who paid.
ev.v_wine_scandal.title: Disgrace at Dinner
ev.v_wine_scandal.text: At an important man's dinner you drank too much and mocked the host in front of everyone. The room went very quiet, and then the whispering began.
ev.v_wine_scandal.text.rome: At an influential Roman's dinner you drank too much, spilled your cup over the dining couch and mocked the host in front of everyone. The slaves froze with their dishes; the guests began to whisper.
ev.v_wine_scandal.apologize: Come back next morning with an apology and a gift
ev.v_wine_scandal.apologize.ok: You were received coldly, but the gift was accepted. The scandal died down — though the invitations stopped.
ev.v_wine_scandal.laugh: Laugh it off: that was the wine talking
ev.v_wine_scandal.laugh.success: Your joke went round the city faster than the gossip. People laugh at you, but kindly.
ev.v_wine_scandal.laugh.failure: The joke didn't help. Now the city calls you 'the one who knows no measure.'
ev.v_wine_scandal.vow: Swear never to drink unmixed wine again
ev.v_wine_scandal.vow.success: You keep your oath. It's harder than you expected: your hand reaches for the jug on its own, and you stop it.
ev.v_wine_scandal.vow.failure: The oath lasted a month. Then there was a festival, then another…
ev.v_wine_missed_work.title: A Heavy Morning
ev.v_wine_missed_work.text: After a night of drinking you slept until noon while the work sat idle and people waited. It isn't the first time, and they've started to look at you sideways.
ev.v_wine_missed_work.makeup: Work into the night to make up for it
ev.v_wine_missed_work.makeup.ok: By nightfall it was all done. Your hands were shaking, but no one can say you let them down.
ev.v_wine_missed_work.lie.success: They believed you and even wished you a quick recovery. The only one you had to face with shame was yourself.
ev.v_wine_missed_work.lie.failure: You'd been seen at the tavern the night before. The lie came out, and half your customers went elsewhere.
ev.v_wine_missed_work.drink: A hair of the dog, and muddle through till evening
ev.v_wine_missed_work.drink.ok: The cup steadied your head but not your hands. The work had to be redone, and people left unhappy.
ev.v_wine_fall.title: The Fall
ev.v_wine_fall.text: Coming home from the tavern at night, you missed a step and tumbled down the stairs. By morning your arm is swollen and your head is splitting.
ev.v_wine_fall.text.rome: Coming home from the popina at night, you missed a step on the steep stairs of your tenement and counted three flights the hard way. By morning your arm is swollen and your head is splitting.
ev.v_wine_fall.physician.ok: The physician set your arm and said bluntly: 'One more fall like that and you won't need me any more.' You nodded without meeting his eyes.
ev.v_wine_fall.poppy: Ask the physician for poppy juice against the pain
ev.v_wine_fall.poppy.ok: The poppy juice eased the pain within the hour. The pain went; the sweet lightness stayed — and you remembered it.
ev.v_wine_fall.endure: Grit your teeth and wash the pain down with wine
ev.v_wine_fall.endure.ok: The wine dulled the pain, but the arm healed crooked. Now it aches whenever rain is coming.
ev.v_wine_quit.title: Giving Up Wine
ev.v_wine_quit.text: One morning you couldn't remember how you got home, and your hands shake until the first sip. It can't go on — but how do you stop?
ev.v_wine_quit.regimen: Ask a physician for a regimen
ev.v_wine_quit.regimen.success: The physician laid it all out: barley gruel, water, long walks, baths and sleep. The first month was torment, but you held on.
ev.v_wine_quit.regimen.failure: For two weeks you dutifully drank barley gruel. In the third you slipped — and were too ashamed to go back to the physician.
ev.v_wine_quit.vow: Make a vow to the gods
ev.v_wine_quit.vow.success: You made your vow at the altar and left an empty jug in the temple. When the craving comes, you remember whom you promised.
ev.v_wine_quit.vow.failure: You broke the vow at the very next festival. Now the craving comes mixed with fear of the gods.
ev.v_wine_quit.friend: Ask a friend not to let you out of sight
ev.v_wine_quit.friend.success: Your friend followed you like a shadow: steered you out of banquets, sat with you in the evenings. Within six months you stopped dreaming of wine.
ev.v_wine_quit.friend.failure: You lied to your friend and hid the jugs. When he realised, he left and slammed the door.
ev.v_wine_quit.later.ok: The jug stays where it is. 'Later' is a very convenient word.
ev.v_wine_relapse.title: Just One Cup
ev.v_wine_relapse.text: At the neighbours' wedding someone holds out a cup of neat wine: 'To the newlyweds! One won't hurt.' Everyone is watching.
ev.v_wine_relapse.one.success: One cup — and you turned it upside down. Even you were surprised at how firm you stayed.
ev.v_wine_relapse.one.failure: One, then a second, then you stopped counting. Within a month everything was back the way it had been.
ev.v_wine_relapse.water: Ask for water and toast the couple with that
ev.v_wine_relapse.water.ok: They teased you all evening. You laughed along with everyone — and went home sober.
ev.v_wine_relapse.leave.ok: The hosts were offended. You know you did the right thing, and it still leaves a bitter taste.
ev.v_wine_sober.text: A whole year without neat wine. Mornings are mornings again: a clear head, steady hands and money that no longer drains away into the tavern.
ev.v_wine_liver.title: The Reckoning
ev.v_wine_liver.text: The whites of your eyes have turned yellow, your belly is swollen, and in the mornings the nausea keeps you in bed. The physician pressed your side for a long time and finally said it plainly: it's the wine.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.success: Fear proved stronger than the craving. The yellow took months to fade, but you never touched unmixed wine again.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.failure: You lasted a week. Your body called for wine louder than the physician's warnings.
ev.v_wine_liver.treat: Take the treatment, but keep drinking a little
ev.v_wine_liver.treat.ok: The physician took the money and only sighed. You felt better — until next winter.
ev.v_wine_liver.ignore: Doctors always try to scare you
ev.v_wine_liver.ignore.ok: You waved it off. The evening cup once again seems like the best medicine.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.title: The Last Word
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.text: {npc} set an empty jug down in front of you: 'It's the wine or me. I'm tired of scrubbing away your shame.'
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.promise.succe: You kept your word. {npc} didn't believe it for a long time, and then one evening silently poured you water at dinner — and smiled.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.promise.failu: The oath lasted until the first festival. Since then the house has been cold, and you don't know how much longer anyone will wait for you.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.temple: Go to the temple together and make a vow
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.temple.succes: You made the vow together, and you kept it together too. It worked.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.temple.failur: The vow was broken within a month. {npc} no longer goes anywhere with you — not to the temple, not to friends.
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.argue: Snap back: 'That's none of your business'
ev.v_wine_spouse_ultimatum.argue.ok: The door slammed. The jug stayed — whether the family stays is no longer up to you.
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.title: Ashamed
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has stopped bringing friends home. You overheard {g=npc_sex:him|her} lying to the neighbours' children: 'Everything's fine at home, we just can't have visitors.'
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.talk.success: You talked half the night. For the sake of those eyes you poured the wine into the gutter — and never bought more.
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.talk.failure: {npc} listened and nodded. You both knew the promise wouldn't last long.
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.angry.ok: You shouted; {npc} said nothing. Friends still never come to the house.
ev.v_wine_child_ashamed.pretend.ok: You kept quiet. Shame moved into the house and now sits at the table with everyone else.
ev.v_dice_first.title: Dice Behind the Tavern
ev.v_dice_first.text: Behind the tavern, by the light of a single lamp, men are throwing dice. The stakes are small, the laughter loud, and they make room for you on the bench.
ev.v_dice_first.text.rome: Behind the popina, out of the aediles' sight, men are throwing dice: gambling for money is banned in Rome except at the Saturnalia, but who cares? They make room for you on the bench.
ev.v_dice_first.small.success: The knucklebones fell in the luckiest throw — all four showing different sides — and you left with a full purse. That night you dreamed of rattling dice.
ev.v_dice_first.small.failure: You lost — not much, but it stings. You itch to win it back.
ev.v_dice_first.big.success: Luck followed you all evening. You raked in a pile of coins and realised nothing in the world fires the blood like this.
ev.v_dice_first.big.failure: In an hour you lost what had taken months to save. Walking out, you were already wondering where to find money for tomorrow's game.
ev.v_dice_first.watch.ok: You watched a few throws and left. Other people's fever looks pitiful from the outside.
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.title: Saturnalia
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.text: Saturnalia! For a week the world is upside down: masters wait on their slaves at table, everyone wears a felt cap, and dice can be thrown in the open without fear of the aediles. The whole household plays for nuts — and some already for coins.
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.nuts.ok: You lost a sack of nuts and won it all back. You haven't laughed like that in ages.
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.coins.success: In the festival week you won more than you'd earn in a month. Shame the Saturnalia is so short…
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.coins.failure: The festival ended, and so did your money. But now you know what the fever smells like.
ev.v_dice_saturnalia.watch.ok: You sat by the brazier watching the game turn sober men into boys. It beat any show in town.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.title: The Big Win
ev.v_dice_bigwin.text: Tonight the dice seem to obey your hand: throw after throw, and the pile of coins in front of you keeps growing. The others scowl and demand one more round.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.stop: Take the winnings and quit for good
ev.v_dice_bigwin.stop.success: You got up from the table and never came back. The winnings went into something useful, not into the next game.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.stop.failure: You left with the money, but a week later you were sitting at the same table again.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.double: One more round — luck's on my side!
ev.v_dice_bigwin.double.success: Luck held: you cleaned out the table to the last coin. The others left cursing — and they'll remember you.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.double.failure: Luck turned as suddenly as it came. You walked out with no winnings and none of your own money.
ev.v_dice_bigwin.feast: Throw a feast with the whole pot
ev.v_dice_bigwin.feast.ok: You treated half the town. By morning all that was left of the winnings was a name for generosity.
ev.v_dice_loss.title: Everything on the Table
ev.v_dice_loss.text: You lost everything: your savings, and then money you didn't have. The winner smiles kindly and expects to be paid by the new moon.
ev.v_dice_loss.borrow: Borrow from a moneylender to pay up
ev.v_dice_loss.borrow.ok: The moneylender counted out the coins without blinking. He named the interest as casually as if he were discussing the weather.
ev.v_dice_loss.sell: Sell everything of value in the house
ev.v_dice_loss.sell.ok: Out went the best dishes, the lamps and your festival cloak. The empty shelves stare at you reproachfully.
ev.v_dice_loss.refuse: Refuse to pay: the game was crooked
ev.v_dice_loss.refuse.success: You raised a cry about a die with lead inside, and the winner, wanting no fuss, backed off. But the gambling dens don't welcome you any more.
ev.v_dice_loss.refuse.failure: Three days later two burly men met you in a dark alley. You paid the debt — and wore the bruises for a long time.
ev.v_dice_collectors.title: The Moneylender's Men
ev.v_dice_collectors.text: Late one evening two men knocked at your door — polite, broad-shouldered, sent by the moneylender. With interest the debt has doubled, and they are done waiting.
ev.v_dice_collectors.pay.ok: You gave them everything you had and borrowed more from the neighbours. The house is bare, but nobody knocks at night any more.
ev.v_dice_collectors.patron.ok: Your patron paid, with a look that would have hurt less as a blow. Now you owe him — and debts like that are never forgotten.
ev.v_dice_collectors.stall.success: They gave you six more months — and promised there would be no second extension.
ev.v_dice_collectors.stall.failure: No extension. They didn't leave empty-handed, and you wore the bruises for a long time.
ev.v_dice_aedile.title: The Raid
ev.v_dice_aedile.text: In the middle of a game the aedile's men burst into the popina. Gambling outside the Saturnalia means a heavy fine — and the shame spreads through the whole quarter.
ev.v_dice_aedile.pay.ok: You paid. Worse, your name was written down, and by the next day the whole street knew it.
ev.v_dice_aedile.bribe.success: The guard acted as if you'd never been there. Convenient memory he has.
ev.v_dice_aedile.bribe.failure: The guard turned out to be honest — a rarity in this city. Now you pay the fine and for the attempted bribe.
ev.v_dice_aedile.run.success: You vaulted the fence and vanished into the alleys. Your heart pounded all the way home.
ev.v_dice_aedile.run.failure: You caught on the fence and crashed right at the guards' feet. A fine, scrapes and roars of laughter.
ev.v_dice_loaded.title: A Loaded Die
ev.v_dice_loaded.text: You noticed that one of your regular opponent's dice almost always lands on six. When you pick it up, it sits too heavy in your palm — lead.
ev.v_dice_loaded.expose: Expose him in front of everyone
ev.v_dice_loaded.expose.success: The players sided with you, and the cheat returned everything he'd won that month. Someone even bought you a drink.
ev.v_dice_loaded.expose.failure: The cheat wasn't alone. You were thrown out the door, and the loaded die vanished along with its owner.
ev.v_dice_loaded.use.success: For a couple of months the lead worked for you. The money came easily, yet meeting the other players' eyes somehow got harder.
ev.v_dice_loaded.use.failure: You were caught on the second night. Now you're the one the city calls a cheat, and they didn't waste many words on you.
ev.v_dice_loaded.quit: Realise the game is a fraud and walk away
ev.v_dice_loaded.quit.success: If the dice lie, what have you been playing all these years? You walked out and never came back.
ev.v_dice_loaded.quit.failure: You moved to another den, where the dice are said to be honest. Said to be.
ev.v_dice_quit.title: Quitting the Dice
ev.v_dice_quit.text: You catch yourself counting other people's purses in your head and seeing dice tumble in your dreams. This can't go on.
ev.v_dice_quit.oath: Swear an oath at the altar
ev.v_dice_quit.oath.success: You swore by the gods and threw your dice into the temple fire. The oath holds tighter than any lock.
ev.v_dice_quit.oath.failure: You broke the oath within a month and now avoid even looking at the temple.
ev.v_dice_quit.purse: Give all your money to someone close for safekeeping
ev.v_dice_quit.purse.success: Now every coin is accounted for, and asking for gambling money is too shameful. A year later you noticed the rattle of dice had left your dreams.
ev.v_dice_quit.purse.failure: You talked the money back out of them on some pretext and lost it in an evening. Trust is harder to win back than money.
ev.v_dice_quit.work: Work so hard there are no free evenings left
ev.v_dice_quit.work.success: Your evenings are filled with work, your purse is filling up, and the gambling den is slowly forgetting your face.
ev.v_dice_quit.work.failure: The work filled your days, but in the evenings your feet carried you to that familiar door.
ev.v_dice_quit.not: One more game — the last one
ev.v_dice_quit.not.ok: The last game turned out to be the second-to-last. Like all the others.
ev.v_dice_relapse.title: Old Friends
ev.v_dice_relapse.text: A former gambling partner recognised you in the street: 'Where've you been hiding? We've got a new table, the stakes are a beauty. One throw, for old times' sake!'
ev.v_dice_relapse.one.success: One throw — and you walked away without looking back. Turns out that's possible too.
ev.v_dice_relapse.one.failure: One throw, then another… By morning you were one of the regulars again.
ev.v_dice_relapse.refuse: Say no and cross to the other side of the street
ev.v_dice_relapse.refuse.ok: He shouted something nasty after you. You didn't turn around.
ev.v_poppy_pain.title: Poppy Juice
ev.v_poppy_pain.text: An old pain in your lower back has kept you awake for months. The physician takes out a vial of thick, dark poppy juice: 'Five drops in wine at night. No more — it's treacherous.'
ev.v_poppy_pain.text.egypt: Your back has kept you awake for months. The healer takes out a vial of dark poppy juice — Theban, the most prized of all: 'Five drops in wine at night. No more — it's treacherous.'
ev.v_poppy_pain.take.ok: For the first time in months you slept until dawn. And you thought that now you knew how to banish any pain. The thought didn't frighten you — it should have.
ev.v_poppy_pain.endure: Endure it: poppy makes people dull
ev.v_poppy_pain.endure.ok: You refused. The pain stayed, but your head stayed your own.
ev.v_poppy_pain.baths: Treat it with baths and rubdowns
ev.v_poppy_pain.baths.ok: Hot water and herb oil work no miracles, but your back is slowly easing.
ev.v_poppy_more.title: A Few More Drops
ev.v_poppy_more.text: Five drops stopped working long ago — you take fifteen now, and without them you can't sleep and snap at everyone. The pain is long gone, yet you need the vial more and more.
ev.v_poppy_more.keep: Keep going: you can't sleep without it
ev.v_poppy_more.keep.ok: The vial took its place by your pillow. Every month you need a new one — and sooner each time.
ev.v_poppy_more.cut.success: For weeks you cut it a drop at a time, sweating through the nights. But one day the vial ran dry, and you didn't buy another.
ev.v_poppy_more.cut.failure: You tried to cut back, but sleepless nights proved more frightening. The drops came back, and there were more of them.
ev.v_poppy_more.physician: Go to a physician for advice
ev.v_poppy_more.physician.success: The physician looked at you carefully and took the vial away. Two hard weeks, and then it got easier.
ev.v_poppy_more.physician.failure: The physician warned you, but the shop next door sells poppy juice with no advice at all.
ev.v_poppy_dreams.text.1: Poppy dreams — slow, warm, golden. You woke toward evening and couldn't remember at first what day it was.
ev.v_poppy_dreams.text.2: More and more often you sit on the threshold staring at nothing. The neighbours have stopped greeting you — they must think you can't hear them anyway.
ev.v_poppy_cost.title: The Price of Forgetting
ev.v_poppy_cost.text: The drug-seller has doubled the price of poppy juice: 'The ships from Egypt are late.' You don't have the money, and without the juice your whole body aches by evening.
ev.v_poppy_cost.text.egypt: The drug-seller has doubled the price of poppy juice: 'The poppy harvest in the Thebaid failed.' You don't have the money, and without the juice your whole body aches by evening.
ev.v_poppy_cost.pay.ok: You paid without haggling. The seller smiled: he knows you'll be back.
ev.v_poppy_cost.household: Take it from the household money
ev.v_poppy_cost.household.ok: You took the money set aside for grain and clothes. Nobody has noticed yet. Yet.
ev.v_poppy_cost.without.success: For three days you shook and retched, for a week you didn't sleep. And then, for the first time in years, your head cleared.
ev.v_poppy_cost.without.failure: On the second day you ran to the seller and paid double. Only the withdrawal was stronger than the craving.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.title: Too Many Drops
ev.v_poppy_overdose.text: You didn't wake in the morning or at noon: they barely roused you by evening, pale and hardly breathing. A few more drops and they wouldn't have roused you at all.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.quit.success: Fear of death proved stronger than the poppy. You smashed the vial on the stones and got through the withdrawal with clenched teeth.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.quit.failure: The fright lasted a week. Then your hands reached for the vial on their own — only now you measure the drops with trembling fingers.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary: Go to the sanctuary of the healing god
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary.success: You spent several nights in the sanctuary, and in a dream the god touched your forehead. In the morning the craving was weaker, and it weakened more each day.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.sanctuary.failure: The dreams in the sanctuary were as poppy-soaked as the ones at home. The god kept silent.
ev.v_poppy_overdose.careful: Just be more careful with the drops
ev.v_poppy_overdose.careful.ok: You measure the drops more carefully. But your hand still wants to add one more.
ev.v_poppy_quit.title: Leaving the Poppy
ev.v_poppy_quit.text: A physician trained in the books of Hippocrates offers to wean you off the poppy: fewer drops each week, baths, barley gruel, walks. He warns you honestly: it will hurt, more than once.
ev.v_poppy_quit.slow: Wean off slowly, under his care
ev.v_poppy_quit.slow.success: Drop by drop, week by week. By spring you realised you hadn't thought of the vial in a long time — and wept with relief.
ev.v_poppy_quit.slow.failure: Halfway there you broke and drank everything you'd hidden away. The physician patiently offered to start again.
ev.v_poppy_quit.sudden.success: The days of withdrawal blurred into one endless, sweat-soaked day. When it ended, you were free.
ev.v_poppy_quit.sudden.failure: Your body rebelled: cramps, fever, sleeplessness. On the fourth day you gave in.
ev.v_poppy_quit.refuse: Refuse: without the poppy life is too grey
ev.v_poppy_quit.refuse.ok: The physician left, shaking his head. The vial by your pillow is full — for now.
ev.v_poppy_relapse.title: The Old Pain
ev.v_poppy_relapse.text: The old injury is aching again with the rains. And in the chest, wrapped in a rag, lies a forgotten vial with the last of the poppy juice.
ev.v_poppy_relapse.drink.success: A few drops — and the vial went back into the chest. You closed the lid and never opened it again.
ev.v_poppy_relapse.drink.failure: A few drops brought it all back: the sweet fog, the craving and a new vial by your pillow.
ev.v_poppy_relapse.pour.ok: You flung the juice into the hearth, and it hissed on the coals. The pain stayed, but the choice was yours.
ev.v_glut_feast.title: A Feast Without Measure
ev.v_glut_feast.text: The host is sparing nothing: eels, fat tuna, roast boar, mountains of honey cakes. You were full long ago, and still the dishes keep coming.
ev.v_glut_feast.text.rome: The host is sparing nothing: dormice in honey and poppy seed, a boar stuffed with live thrushes, oysters from the Lucrine Lake. You were full long ago, and still the dishes keep coming.
ev.v_glut_feast.text.egypt: The host is sparing nothing: roast geese and pigeons, dates in honey, beer and wine flowing freely. You were full long ago, and still the dishes keep coming.
ev.v_glut_feast.all: Try everything — you were invited, after all
ev.v_glut_feast.all.ok: You ate until you could no longer tell one taste from another. Back home your own table suddenly looked poor — and you started wondering about setting one like that.
ev.v_glut_feast.measure.ok: You tried a morsel of each and pushed the plate away. The host was offended; your stomach was grateful.
ev.v_glut_feast.napkin: Wrap some treats in your napkin to take home
ev.v_glut_feast.napkin.ok: Plenty of guests do it: treats in a napkin are fair spoils. At home you were greeted like a hero.
ev.v_glut_gout.title: Gout
ev.v_glut_gout.text: Your big toe has swollen and burns so badly that even the touch of a sheet is unbearable. The physician nods: gout — the disease of the well-fed, and feasts are what feed it.
ev.v_glut_gout.diet.success: Barley porridge, vegetables and water instead of banquets. Six months later your foot fit into a sandal again.
ev.v_glut_gout.diet.failure: You lasted a month, and then friends threw a feast. Your foot reminded you of it that same night.
ev.v_glut_gout.poppy: Dull the pain with poppy juice
ev.v_glut_gout.poppy.ok: Poppy juice takes the pain away within the hour. It doesn't cure the gout — but you'd rather not think about that.
ev.v_glut_gout.physician.ok: Compresses, a strict regimen, bitter draughts. It wasn't cheap, but the attack passed.
ev.v_greed_famine.title: Grain in a Hungry Year
ev.v_greed_famine.text: The harvest failed and grain prices have soared. Your granary is full, and one by one the neighbours come to ask — on credit, until better times.
ev.v_greed_famine.sell: Sell it at triple the price in the market
ev.v_greed_famine.sell.ok: You grew rich in a single winter. But people now greet you in the street through clenched teeth.
ev.v_greed_famine.usury: Lend it out at steep interest
ev.v_greed_famine.usury.ok: The neighbours took the grain and signed the notes. In spring you'll get yours back with plenty extra — and their quiet hatred thrown in.
ev.v_greed_famine.share: Let it go at the old, fair price
ev.v_greed_famine.share.ok: You sold the grain at last year's price. Little profit, but the district won't forget this winter.
ev.v_greed_famine.hoard: Hold on: prices will climb higher
ev.v_greed_famine.hoard.success: You waited for spring and sold it all at an unthinkable price. Wealth smells of grain — and of other people's hunger.
ev.v_greed_famine.hoard.failure: The grain got damp and mouldy in the granary. No money, no gratitude — only the smell of rot and gossip.
ev.v_rage_home.title: The Outburst
ev.v_rage_home.text: It had been a bad day, and at home some small thing set you off — spilled soup. You slammed your fist on the table so hard the bowls flew to the floor, and the household froze.
ev.v_rage_home.apologize.ok: You picked up the shards and apologised. Dinner was finished in silence, but the ice slowly melted.
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet: Recite the whole alphabet to yourself, as the philosophers advise
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet.success: Alpha, beta, gamma… by omega the anger was gone. Turns out the philosophers know a thing or two.
ev.v_rage_home.alphabet.failure: You got as far as epsilon and blew up again. Letters are no match for rage.
ev.v_rage_home.blame.ok: You shouted until you were hoarse. You felt better — and ever since, the household speaks in low voices.
ev.v_rage_child.title: The Shadow of Anger
ev.v_rage_child.text: You've noticed that your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} flinches whenever you raise your voice and won't meet your eyes. When did that start?
ev.v_rage_child.change: Hold yourself back, whatever it takes
ev.v_rage_child.change.success: It was hard, but {npc} laughs around you again. Sometimes you catch that old, trusting look.
ev.v_rage_child.change.failure: You held it together for a month, then blew up again. {npc} doesn't flinch any more — {g=npc_sex:he|she} just leaves the room.
ev.v_rage_child.talk.ok: You explained that you shout from tiredness, not from lack of love. {npc} listened in silence: words weigh less than deeds, for now.
ev.v_rage_child.strict: A firm hand never hurt anyone
ev.v_rage_child.strict.ok: That's how you were raised, and that's how you raise. {npc} is growing up quiet and distant.
ev.v_theft_chance.title: Someone Else's Till
ev.v_theft_chance.text: The one you work for left you in charge of the takings and went away for a week. The coins lie in the chest, nobody has counted them, and payday is a long way off. You've also noticed your workmate already dipping into it.
ev.v_theft_chance.take: Take a little — no one will notice
ev.v_theft_chance.take.ok: You took just a little. Then a little more. It's a big chest, after all.
ev.v_theft_chance.honest.ok: The owner counted every last coin and was pleased. Trust is capital too.
ev.v_theft_chance.report.success: The owner thanked you and raised your pay. Your workmate was thrown out that same day.
ev.v_theft_chance.report.failure: The owner didn't believe you, and your workmate found out who informed on him. Now you have an enemy.
ev.v_theft_caught.title: The Accounts Don't Add Up
ev.v_theft_caught.text: Your employer went over several years of records, and the shortfall is too large to blame on mice. He is looking straight at you.
ev.v_theft_caught.confess: Confess and pay it all back
ev.v_theft_caught.confess.ok: You returned every last coin, and it never came to court. But such things aren't forgotten: the sideways looks lingered for years.
ev.v_theft_caught.deny.success: No proof turned up. He backed down, but he never leaves you alone with the money again.
ev.v_theft_caught.deny.failure: Witnesses and records turned up. You had to repay double, and word of your sticky fingers spread through the whole quarter.
ev.v_theft_caught.blame.success: Someone else was punished. You got away with it… but sleep is slow to come at night.
ev.v_theft_caught.blame.failure: The lie came out, and now you're not only a thief but a slanderer.
ev.v_fraud_weights.title: Light Weights
ev.v_fraud_weights.text: A merchant you know shows you weights filed down underneath: 'Every customer gets a pinch less — and by year's end you've earned yourself a new house.'
ev.v_fraud_weights.use: Take a couple of those weights
ev.v_fraud_weights.use.ok: Takings went up and the customers noticed nothing. So far.
ev.v_fraud_weights.refuse.ok: The merchant shrugged: 'Honest folk don't last.' But your scales still tell the truth.
ev.v_fraud_weights.report.success: The inspector smashed the filed weights in front of the whole market. The traders eye you warily; the customers, with respect.
ev.v_fraud_weights.report.failure: The merchant denied everything, and the inspector just shrugged. Now you have an enemy in the market.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.title: Inspection at the Market
ev.v_fraud_exposed.text: The market inspector is walking down the rows with a balance, checking every weight. He's three stalls from yours.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.text.athens: The agoranomos, the market inspector, is walking down the rows with the standard weights, checking each one. He's three stalls from yours.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.text.rome: The aedile's men are walking down the rows with the standard measures, checking every weight. They're three stalls from yours.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.swap.success: The filed weights vanished under the counter a moment before the check. The inspector walked on. Your knees shook for an hour.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.swap.failure: The inspector caught the movement. The weights were smashed in front of everyone, you were fined, and word spread through the market: they cheat at that stall.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.confess.ok: The fine was smaller than it might have been: the inspector values honesty, even a late one.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.blame: Blame it all on your assistant
ev.v_fraud_exposed.blame.success: The assistant was dismissed and you got off with a scare. Only the assistant had nothing to do with it.
ev.v_fraud_exposed.blame.failure: The assistant didn't stay quiet and told everything he knew. Now you pay — for the cheating and for the false accusation.
ev.v_vanity_purple.title: Purple
ev.v_vanity_purple.text: The cloth merchant has a cloak dyed with genuine Tyrian purple. It costs as much as a craftsman earns in a year, but in it you'd look like someone people envy.
ev.v_vanity_purple.buy: Buy it — you only live once
ev.v_vanity_purple.buy.ok: The cloak fits magnificently. You catch admiring looks on every street — and you're already thinking what to buy to go with it.
ev.v_vanity_purple.fake.ok: You can't tell from a distance. Or up close — unless you know. You hope not many people know.
ev.v_vanity_purple.pass.ok: You walked on. Someone will buy the cloak — someone for whom seeming matters more than being.
ev.v_lust_brothel.title: The House with the Lamp
ev.v_lust_brothel.text: Your friends want to go and 'unwind' at the house with the lamp over its door. The madam calls from the threshold, and deep inside, behind the curtains, are girls nobody here ever asked about anything.
ev.v_lust_brothel.go.ok: The evening was loud and empty. On the way home your friends boasted, and for some reason you wanted to wash.
ev.v_lust_brothel.home.ok: Your friends laughed. You shrugged and went home to bed.
ev.v_lust_brothel.talk: Talk to one of the girls — just talk
ev.v_lust_brothel.talk.ok: Her real name isn't the one the madam calls her. She comes from far away and barely remembers home. You left with a heavy heart.
ev.v_lust_affair.title: Another's Glance
ev.v_lust_affair.text: Someone on the next street has long been trying to catch your eye, and today they invited you in while no one else is home. And at your own home {npc} is waiting — as every evening.
ev.v_lust_affair.yes.ok: It was like a gulp of unmixed wine: sweet, heady and unsettling. You came home late, with an excuse made up on the way.
ev.v_lust_affair.no.ok: You walked past the stranger's door. At home {npc} asked why you looked so thoughtful.
ev.v_lust_affair.smile: Give a smile — and nothing more
ev.v_lust_affair.smile.ok: A smile costs nothing and promises nothing. You walked on feeling younger.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.title: It Came Out
ev.v_lust_affair_found.text: The neighbours talked: {npc} knows everything. {g=npc_sex:He|She} isn't shouting — just sitting in the dark, waiting for what you'll say.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.beg.success: Forgiveness came slowly and not completely. But one morning {npc} set your cup on the table again.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.beg.failure: There was no forgiveness. A month later the marriage was dissolved before witnesses, and half the house stood empty.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.deny.success: You were believed — or at least it was made to look that way. Now you both have to live with it.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.deny.failure: The lie only made it worse. A month later the marriage was dissolved before witnesses, and the neighbours had a story for years.
ev.v_lust_affair_found.leave.ok: You packed that same night. The door closed quietly behind you — the way doors close when they won't open again.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.title: Someone Else's Luck
ev.v_envy_neighbor.text: The neighbour who once started out level with you has bought a second house and now travels by litter. Every time you pass his gate, something burns under your ribs.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.curse: Commission a curse on a lead tablet
ev.v_envy_neighbor.curse.ok: The sorcerer scratched your neighbour's name on a lead tablet, rolled it up and dropped it down a well. You felt better — though the neighbour doesn't seem to have noticed.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.rumor: Start a rumour about where his money came from
ev.v_envy_neighbor.rumor.success: The rumour took root: now the whole quarter talks about him. Strangely, it brought you no joy.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.rumor.failure: The rumour was quickly traced back to you. Now people talk about your envy instead.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.work.ok: You work from dawn till dark. You haven't caught up with him yet, but the burning under your ribs has eased.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.ask: Drop by and ask how he did it
ev.v_envy_neighbor.ask.success: He turned out not to be proud at all, but generous with advice. You talked late into the night and, it seems, became friends.
ev.v_envy_neighbor.ask.failure: He answered curtly and from on high. You left feeling you'd humbled yourself for nothing.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.title: Cup After Cup
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.text: {npc} pours neat wine before sunset more and more often, and the jars in the storeroom empty faster than you can buy new ones.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.talk.success: You talked into the night. It turned out the wine was hiding a sadness you hadn't known about. The jars empty more slowly now.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.talk.failure: {npc} took offence and shut down. There's no less wine in the house.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.hide: Hide the wine and water it down in secret
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.hide.ok: You started cutting the wine three to one. Time will tell whether the trick works.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.ignore: Stay out of it: everyone drinks as they please
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink.ignore.ok: You said nothing. After all, who doesn't drink in the evenings? Only the evenings kept getting longer.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.title: Drinking the House Away
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.text: {npc} pawned your best cloak and the silver cup from the dowry at the tavern. The neighbours whisper, and at night the house swings between shouting and heavy silence.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} to a physician and the temple, whatever it costs
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician.su: Months of regimen, vows and sleepless nights. One day {npc} poured the wine into the gutter unprompted — and you wept with relief.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.physician.fa: The physician tried, the priests prayed, but within a month it was all back. The money is gone, and there's less hope left.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.divorce.ok: The marriage was dissolved before witnesses. The house is quiet and empty, and for the first time in years you sleep until morning.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.endure: Endure it and hide the shame
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_later.endure.ok: You redeemed the cloak and the cup and told the neighbours everything was fine. You've become very good at lying.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_end.text: In winter {npc} took to bed and never rose again: the liver, the physician said, had been failing for a long time. The wine that promised relief took everything. The house is quiet, and you can't tell whether grief or guilt weighs on you more.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_moment.text.1: {npc} came home past midnight again, stumbling over the threshold. You pretended to be asleep.
ev.v_rel_spouse_drink_moment.text.2: At dinner {npc} drained a third cup of neat wine and launched into a song. You finished your meal alone in the courtyard.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.title: Wagers
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.text: {npc} keeps disappearing to the cockfights, coming home sometimes with a handful of coins, sometimes empty-handed with shifty eyes. Yesterday the tax money vanished from the chest.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.text.rome: {npc} keeps disappearing to the Circus Maximus, betting on the Greens as if the fate of Rome depended on it. Yesterday the tax money vanished from the chest.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.text.athens: {npc} keeps disappearing to the quail fights, coming home sometimes with a handful of coins, sometimes empty-handed with shifty eyes. Yesterday the tax money vanished from the chest.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.confront.success: It was a hard talk, but an honest one. {npc} promised to forget the way to the betting — and seems to be keeping the promise.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.confront.failure: {npc} denied everything, and a week later more went missing from the chest.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.lock: Lock up the money and wear the key round your neck
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.lock.ok: The key never leaves you now. {npc} looks at it as if you were the guilty one.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.join: Go together and see what the thrill is about
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.join.success: You placed one bet — and won. You came home laughing like when you were young. If only it doesn't become a habit.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races.join.failure: You both lost. Worse — you enjoyed it.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.title: A Spouse's Debts
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.text: A moneylender came to you with a note: {npc} borrowed against your house. It's due by the end of the month.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.pay.ok: You handed over everything saved for your old age. {npc} swears never again. You've heard that oath before.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.condition: Pay it — but no more betting, ever
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.condition.su: The debt is cleared, and betting is strictly forbidden. {npc} is holding to it — with something like relief.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.condition.fa: You cleared the debt, but the ban held only until the next races. It's all happening again.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.divorce: Dissolve the marriage and disown the debts
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.divorce.ok: You renounced both the marriage and someone else's notes. The house was saved; the family wasn't.
ev.v_rel_spouse_races_later.refuse.ok: The moneylender left unhappy, and {npc} left in tears. How it will end is still unclear.
ev.v_rel_child_dice.title: A Dice Debt
ev.v_rel_child_dice.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came to you pale: {g=npc_sex:he|she} lost more at dice than everything {g=npc_sex:he|she} owns, and the winner wants the money by market day.
ev.v_rel_child_dice.pay.ok: You paid in silence. {npc} hugged you — and seemed to calm down a little too quickly.
ev.v_rel_child_dice.work: Lend it — and make {g=npc_sex:him|her} work it off
ev.v_rel_child_dice.work.ok: You lent the money on strict terms. For a whole year {npc} worked without a break and seems to have learned the lesson.
ev.v_rel_child_dice.refuse: Refuse: let {g=npc_sex:him|her} get out of it alone
ev.v_rel_child_dice.refuse.ok: {npc} left, slamming the door. They say {g=npc_sex:he|she} borrowed from people one shouldn't borrow from.
ev.v_rel_child_debt.title: Creditors at the Gate
ev.v_rel_child_debt.text: The people {npc} owes have come to your house: your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} has been gambling again, lost again — and named you as guarantor.
ev.v_rel_child_debt.pay: Pay up, for the last time
ev.v_rel_child_debt.pay.ok: You paid, telling yourself it was the last time. {npc} told {g=npc_sex:himself|herself} the same thing.
ev.v_rel_child_debt.ultimatum.success: 'One more throw and you'll never cross this threshold again.' {npc} believed you. Dice never appeared in {g=npc_sex:his|her} hands again.
ev.v_rel_child_debt.ultimatum.failure: The condition held until the next festival. You already know what comes next.
ev.v_rel_child_debt.disown: Publicly refuse to answer for {g=npc_sex:his|her} debts
ev.v_rel_child_debt.disown.ok: You declared before witnesses that you no longer answer for those debts. The creditors backed off. So did {npc}: {g=npc_sex:he|she} stopped coming by.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.title: Home at Dawn
ev.v_rel_child_wine.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came home at dawn, swaying, and fumbled at the bolt for ages. Now {g=npc_sex:he|she} is pale and won't meet your eyes.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.story: Tell the honest story of your own drinking
ev.v_rel_child_wine.story.ok: You told it all, unvarnished. {npc} listened without interrupting. It seems the lesson sank in.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.talk: Explain how decent people drink: with water and in moderation
ev.v_rel_child_wine.talk.success: {npc} nodded, wincing from the headache. You never saw neat wine in {g=npc_sex:his|her} cup again.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.talk.failure: {npc} nodded along — and next time simply came home more quietly.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.punish.ok: The punishment was harsh. {npc} didn't stop drinking — just got better at hiding it.
ev.v_rel_child_wine.laugh: Laugh it off: everyone's been there
ev.v_rel_child_wine.laugh.ok: You laughed and poured {g=npc_sex:him|her} some water. The laughter eased the awkwardness — but not the question.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.title: A Regular
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.text: {npc}, your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter}, spends more and more time at the tavern instead of at work. Yesterday strangers carried {g=npc_sex:him|her} home.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.help: Take it seriously: physician, regimen, supervision
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.help.success: It cost money, strength and many quarrels. But a year later {npc} is up at dawn again and looks you in the eye.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.help.failure: The regimen lasted a month. {npc} resents being watched — and drinks out of spite.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.cut.success: With no money, the tavern closed its doors on its own. {npc} was angry for a long time, and then said thank you.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.cut.failure: {npc} started drinking on credit. Now there are creditors on top of the drinking.
ev.v_rel_child_wine_later.cover.ok: You told the neighbours {npc} was just a little unwell. The neighbours nodded. The neighbours knew.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.title: Blood Kin
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.text: Your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} is at the door — puffy-faced, in someone else's cloak, reeking of wine. {g=npc_sex:He|She} asks for a little money, 'just until tomorrow.'
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.give.ok: 'Until tomorrow' stretched into forever. You knew it as you handed over the coins.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.takein: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} in and keep the wine away
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.takein.success: For a month {npc} raged, cursed and wept. And then one morning asked not for wine, but for work.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.takein.failure: A week later {npc} slipped away in the night with your purse. You're left with anger and pity in equal parts.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink.refuse.ok: You closed the door and stood leaning against it for a long time. The footsteps outside took a while to fade.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.title: A Cold Night
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.text: Word came: {npc} fell asleep drunk in the street on a freezing night and now lies in a fever. The healer says {g=npc_sex:he|she} might live, with care.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.nurse.success: For weeks you barely left the bedside. {npc} lived — and, having looked death in the eye, gave up drinking.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.nurse.failure: You did everything you could. On the tenth morning {npc} stopped breathing — quietly, as if just falling asleep.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.pay: Pay for a healer and a nurse
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.pay.success: {npc} recovered. {g=npc_sex:He|She} didn't stop drinking, but sent you thanks through the neighbours.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.pay.failure: The money didn't save {g=npc_sex:him|her}. The nurse said {npc} kept calling for you until the end.
ev.v_rel_sibling_drink_end.stay.ok: You didn't go. You learned how it ended later — and it was hard to hear.
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.title: Footsteps at the Door
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.text: You can already tell from his footsteps how much your father has drunk. Tonight they are heavy and uneven, and {npc} is looking for someone to take it out on before he's even through the door.
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.hide.ok: The neighbour silently made up a bench for you. It has happened before, and she asks no questions.
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.calm.success: You took off his sandals and covered him with his cloak. He mumbled about how sorry he was. He won't remember it in the morning.
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.calm.failure: He shoved you so hard you hit the wall. He won't remember it in the morning — but you will.
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.roam: Slip out and wander until dawn
ev.v_rel_father_drunk.roam.ok: You wandered the dark streets until dawn. The city at night is frightening, but no more than home.
ev.v_rel_father_old.title: The Old Man and the Wine
ev.v_rel_father_old.text: {npc} has aged and weakened: his hands shake, his eyes are cloudy, and he talks more and more about the past. Yesterday he called for you and said he wants to ask your forgiveness — for those nights.
ev.v_rel_father_old.forgive.ok: You took his trembling hand. The weight you've carried since childhood grew a little lighter.
ev.v_rel_father_old.care: Don't forgive, but look after him
ev.v_rel_father_old.care.ok: You can't forgive him. But you bring him soup and change his bedding — because it has to be done.
ev.v_rel_father_old.leave.ok: You left. Some wounds words cannot close.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.title: Sleeping Drops
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.text: {npc} has taken poppy juice for her aching joints for years, and now she takes it with no pain at all. She dozes through the day, and by evening she is searching for the vial with shaking hands.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.physician.success: The physician talked with her long and gently, then told her to cut back drop by drop. Within six months the vial was gone from the shelf.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.physician.failure: The physician left, and {npc} was only angry: 'It's medicine, not wine.' The drops stayed.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.hide.success: For two weeks {npc} wouldn't speak to you. Then, for the first time in years, she came to breakfast with clear eyes.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.hide.failure: She found another shop. Now you both pretend nothing is happening.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.let: Leave it be: it makes things easier for her
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy.let.ok: It really does make things easier for her. Only each month there's less of the person you knew.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.title: The Long Sleep
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.text: {npc} barely gets up any more, doesn't recognise the neighbours and calls you by someone else's name. The physician is blunt: her heart can't take the poppy, but without it she will be in great pain.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.wean: Wean her off, however hard it is
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.wean.success: Those were the hardest months of your life. But in spring {npc} stepped out into the courtyard and knew you.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.wean.failure: Her heart could bear neither the poppy nor its loss. {npc} slipped away quietly in her sleep, holding your hand.
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.comfort: Don't torment her: let her be free of pain
ev.v_rel_mother_poppy_end.comfort.ok: You sat beside her and held her hand. There was no pain — only a long, quiet sleep.
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.title: Standing Surety
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.text: {npc}, your old friend, has lost at dice and asks you to stand surety for {g=npc_sex:him|her} with a moneylender: 'I'll pay it all back in six months, by the gods!'
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.vouch.success: {npc} really did pay it all back — on time, to the last coin. The friendship passed the test of silver.
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.vouch.failure: Six months later the moneylender came to you for the money. {npc} avoids your eyes and mutters that it'll all be paid back any day now.
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.part: Give a little of your own, but don't vouch
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.part.ok: You gave what you could spare. {npc} thanked you — a little more coolly than you expected.
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.refuse: Refuse: gambling and friendship don't mix
ev.v_rel_friend_surety.refuse.ok: {npc} took offence and didn't speak to you for a week. But your purse is intact.
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.title: A Friend at Rock Bottom
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.text: {npc} has lost everything: the house, the workshop, even the cloak. The creditors are threatening court and bondage until the debt is worked off, and {g=npc_sex:he|she} has come to you — there's no one else.
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.pay.success: You bought out the debt. {npc} wept on your shoulder and never picked up dice again.
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.pay.failure: You bought out the debt. A year later {npc} was seen in the gambling den again.
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.shelter: Offer a roof and work, but no money
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.shelter.ok: A corner of the house and work to do. {npc} grumbles but works — and the creditors wait.
ev.v_rel_friend_ruin.refuse.ok: You refused. You never saw each other again: they say the creditors took the debtor away to work it off.
